target_customer: Casual online gamers (teens and young adults), monetized via ads and virtual goods; later mobile players of Draw Something
problem: Casual players wanted quick social multiplayer games; OMGPOP built real-time Flash games and later mobile social games, and the founder started with a dating auction joke.
business_model: advertising and virtual goods in free games, later paid and ad-supported mobile games

founders.name: Charles Forman
founders.role: founder and CEO until Dan Porter replaced him
founders.background_notes: Started in SoHo, New York as iminlikewithyou; later left and Dan Porter became CEO; had about $1,700 in the bank before the Zynga deal per TechSpot headline

competitors.name: Miniclip and Addicting Games
competitors.what: Flash game portals that had been around for several years
competitors.traction_then: tens of millions of young users

competitors.name: Kongregate
competitors.what: Flash game portal launched 2006 with revenue share for developers

technical_complexity.rationale: Flash multiplayer games and a mobile drawing game are modest engineering; the hard part was scaling Draw Something servers during a viral spike.

defensibility.rationale: Game mechanics were trivially copyable, and Draw Something's usage fell after clones and the acquisition.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Zynga bought OMGPOP in March 2012 and shut the studio in June 2013.

market_need_then: Flash game portals drew tens of millions of young users in 2006 to 2007; social game demand later boomed on Facebook and iPhone.

branding.name_origin: Started as iminlikewithyou, a joke dating auction site, renamed OMGPOP when it focused on games; no source explains the name itself.
branding.brand_signature: Draw Something, which downloaded over 35 million times in six weeks per Zynga's announcement

rebrands.why: Shifted from the dating auction idea to games (date approximate, unverified)

branding.community_and_virality: Om Malik titled a post 'a real OMG pop' on the Zynga sale; Draw Something went viral.

brand_strength.rationale: Draw Something was more famous than the company name, and the brand ended with the Zynga shutdown.

pivots.why: Games drew users; the dating idea started as a near joke per a secondary source

pivots.to: mobile social games, including Draw Something
pivots.why: Mobile and social games were growing; Draw Something launched Feb 2012

outcome_analysis: OMGPOP survived near-insolvency in 2011 with a $10.1M rescue round, then struck gold with Draw Something in February 2012 and sold to Zynga in March for a reported $180M to $210M. Usage fell fast after the deal, the founder and CEO left, and Zynga closed the studio in June 2013, so the exit was strong for investors but the product and team did not last.
notes: omgpop.com did not resolve in this environment (DNS error). Acquisition price conflicts: $180M, $200M, $210M including retention (Fortune), so null. Seed and Series A amounts not found. Total VC reported as $16.6M or $17M. The 2011 round of $10.1M listed officially as Series B-1 by Fortune and as Series B by Global Venturing. YC lists only Charles Forman as founder. Dates of the rename and Forman's departure not sourced. Founder education and prior jobs not found. OMGPOP was closed by Zynga June 2013 as part of 520 layoffs per press, so directory status Acquired is consistent with the 2012 acquisition.
